notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); no hardware was attached and no hardware run is claimed. WHAT IT SERVES: the card's models[0], assets/trlc_dk1/scene_blocks.xml, as a MujocoDriver in simulated mode R0, device kind world.sim. cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [16 numbers]}}; the bridge checks every ctrl element against the model's actuator_ctrlrange before data.ctrl is written, then runs mj_step ticks times. The 16 channels are six joint position actuators and two gripper position actuators per arm; the joint ranges are +-2.0944, -0.0872665 to 3.14159, -0.0872665 to 4.71239, -1.95 to 1.5708, +-1.5708 and +-2.0944, and the gripper ranges are -0.045 to 0.001 (scene_blocks.xml:300-315). cap.world.reset.v1 restores the data with mj_resetData + mj_forward. The state is the bridge integration state (time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed); the scene has 37 qpos and 34 qvel values (12 hinge joints, 4 gripper slides and 3 free bodies). No Limit is declared: the envelope is derived from the model at run time; there is no site-limits.example.json and no operator-required bound. WHY THIS SHAPE: the card is family-config with helper MujocoDriver, and the upstream artifacts are committed MJCF scenes (README.md:325-327); the card has no entry_symbols. The model is read from the read-only clone in place and is never copied into the package or imported. Only models[0] is served; scene_dishes.xml is the other environment, and the teleop, WebXR, capture and training stacks are not part of this driver. NOT COVERED: MuJoCo was not importable where the gate ran (no network, no pip), so backends['fake'] is this package's stand-in mujoco module (fake.py). It parses the same MJCF for the 16 control ranges, the joint dimensions and the option timestep, but its integration is a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated joint toward its control value; it loads no mesh, texture, material or inertia, resolves no contact, friction, tendon, equality or actuator constraint, and resets qpos to zero rather than model qpos0. The model sets no timestep (scene_blocks.xml:4), so the published timestep_ms 2.0 is the stand-in's # placeholder library default, not a sourced fact; it is test data and appears in no Fact or Limit. No trajectory was compared with the real engine; the real sim path (the official mujoco module loading the same scene) was not run. No viewer, rendering or camera stream is exposed; the scene cameras and HDRI backdrop are not served. No physical TRLC DK1 arm is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware. WARNINGS (none failed): G8.NO_UNIT x3 for ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed, which PLAYBOOK.md section 8 calls expected for MuJoCo drivers; G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because backends['fake'] is a package stand-in for the mujoco module rather than a package class the gate can wrap in a Recorder. No G4.REF_VALUE, G4.REF_BINARY, G4.REF_MISSING or G4.REF_LINE warning was raised. TESTS: test_driver.py keeps mhs.testing.check_driver and adds six cases (model shape from the blocks scene; per-channel control-range refusals with zero effect; a step moving a joint and reaching the stand-in; reset to the stand-in defaults; the published fidelity contract; the e-stop latch); they pass. No catalogue_requests: only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 are used.
